headline: Physics-coupled inference recovers hidden biophysical parameters from indirect data
label: Biological Dynamics Modeling Frameworks
summary: Simulation- and physics-embedded estimators now extract cell, filament, and molecular parameters from microscopy, trajectory, and force data.
synthesis: The common thread across these four preprints is inverse inference: unobserved physical parameters are recovered from indirect measurements by coupling a mechanistic or simulation-based model with a learning or Bayesian estimator. OptiCell3D infers cell mechanical properties from 3D microscopy through simulations and backpropagation-based optimization. A diffusion model trained on coarse-grained actin curvature and density heatmaps from simulated actomyosin networks predicts cortical flow at unseen filament turnover. DeepDiffusion, a physics-informed neural network, estimates instantaneous diffusion along single-molecule trajectories of DNA-binding proteins. A Bayesian framework infers vimentin bond parameters from optical-tweezers force trajectories and identifies an optimal pulling velocity. What is new is the explicit embedding of physical constraints or simulation outputs directly into the inference pipeline.
